note: Read 2026-11-01 at the owner's word ("Build those first 3 starting with ledger first"; of the 21 countries read first: "It should cover across every country"; "Retry the blocked tax facts once all countries land"): the tax on a screen worker's pay in Libya: a resident's income tax, social contributions, what is withheld at source, a non-resident artiste's withholding, an author's treatment, VAT and the tax year. Research and retry subagents (workbench/briefs/BRIEF-tax.md, BRIEF-tax-retry.md), every quote checked by the lead against its saved page.

figures.finding: Libyan and foreign nationals alike pay tax only on Libyan-source income: employment income is taxed at 5% on annual taxable earnings up to LYD 12,000 and 10% above, after social security, the 1% solidarity contribution and a personal exemption of LYD 1,800 (single) or 2,400 (married), plus LYD 300 a child; professional or commercial income is taxed at 15%.

sources.said: Gross salary Tax rate (%) Per year (LYD*) Per month (LYD) 12,000 1,000 5 Over 12,000 Over 1,000 10

Income earned from commercial activities is subject to a 15% rate and income from handicrafts is taxed at 10%. Payroll tax is imposed at 5% on annual taxable earnings up to LYD 12,000 and at 10% on annual taxable earnings exceeding LYD 12,000. … An annual allowance of LYD 1,800 (for a single individual) or LYD 2,400 (for a married or widowed adult) may be deducted from taxable income. In addition, an annual allowance of LYD 300 is provided for each minor child.

figures.finding: Everyone working in Libya, expatriates included, pays social security of 5.125% of gross income; the employer pays 14.350% (15.375% for a foreign branch), with 1.025% from the treasury for Libyan entities; a further 1% of monthly gross salary goes to the Social Unity Fund.

value.due: within ten days after month end

sources.said: Gross income Foreign branch (%) Libyan entity (%) Employee’s contribution 5.125 5.125 Employer’s contribution 15.375 14.350 Contribution from public treasury - 1.025 Total 20.50 20.50 … Social security is withheld by the employer and payable monthly, within ten days after the month end. … 1% of the monthly gross salary of all individuals exercising employment in Libya is collected by the Tax Department as a contribution to the Social Unity Fund.

figures.finding: The employer withholds tax on employment income at the employee's rate and remits it within 60 days of the month end (plus 15 days' grace).

value.due: 60 days after month end + 15 days grace

sources.said: Tax on employment income is withheld and remitted by the employer at the individual’s applicable rate. The employer is responsible for monthly filing and the due date is 60 days following the end of the month (plus a 15-day grace period).

figures.finding: Residence does not decide liability: a foreign performer working in Libya pays the same tax on Libyan-source income; Libyan law has no withholding taxes, foreign contracts being assessed on deemed profit at registration.

sources.said: Residence is not a key factor in determining tax liability in Libya, which is typically based on the source of income (particularly for non-Libyan nationals).
Libyan law has no withholding taxes (WHTs).

figures.finding: There is no VAT in Libya.

sources.said: There is no VAT in Libya.

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; payroll is self-assessed monthly through the employer.

sources.said: The tax year is a calendar year. Tax returns The submission of the monthly declared payroll is effectively a self-assessment process.

figures.finding: Income from writing books and from preparing studies and research in culture and science is exempt from income tax (Law No. 7 of 2010, art. 33); other income of an independent profession is taxed at 15% a year (arts. 53 and 54).

value.exempt: income from writing books and preparing cultural or scientific studies and research

figures.applies: Individuals, Law No. 7 of 2010 as in force (amended by Law No. 2 of 2017 and Law No. 1 of 2025, each in art. 25 only, as the portal lists them). The exemption names books, studies and research, not a script; the game applies neither it nor the professions' 15% (the business tax is already untold), and tells the player the author's relief isn't kept.
